severity_rationale: C4 Low/QA: precision/rounding state-handling issue. Conservation of budget holds; the described drift is sub-second and sub-unit over individual pulls. The soft-MEV timing surface requires sophisticated searcher infrastructure and mempool observation, and the profit scale is bounded by a small fraction of a single reset's delta. No direct theft, no value permanently lost. Classified Low because it is a rounding / state-handling issue per C4 criteria.
title: _applyAsymmetricWindow integer divisions in extend-branch and candidate computation silently under-account small inflows and budget changes
description: Two integer divisions in _applyAsymmetricWindow lose precision in ways that affect both runway accounting and rate-change timing: (1) Extend-branch: windowEnd += inflow / rewardRate. When inflow < rewardRate (common for dispatcher-hook drizzle), the extension rounds to zero but rewardBudget still grows. Small, frequent pulls accumulate budget without proportionally extending the window. (2) Candidate boundary: candidate = rewardBudget / windowDuration is integer-floored. For any rewardBudget in [k*windowDuration, (k+1)*windowDuration), candidate = k; the fractional inflow contributes budget but not rate. Consequences: (a) windowEnd becomes an unreliable runway indicator, occasionally triggering scheduleExpired resets earlier than the protocol should. (b) When accumulated under-extended budget eventually tips candidate above rewardRate (possibly via a single later pull), a 'saved-up rate jump' fires at a time determined by the cadence of hook pulls — creating an MEV timing surface. Stakers present at the reset moment benefit; stakers who exited just before do not. A mempool-aware observer can time stakes around the predicted reset.
attack_path:
Accounting drift: 1) rewardRate = 1e18 phUSD/sec. 2) Dispatcher hook drizzles 1e17-sized mint-debt batches every few stake/unstake calls. 3) Each _syncBudget inflow extends windowEnd by 0; budget accumulates. 4) Eventually scheduleExpired prematurely fires on a subsequent call (windowEnd advanced by fewer seconds than budget should have afforded), resetting rate at an unintended time.

MEV timing: 1) Observer monitors rewardBudget / windowDuration vs rewardRate on-chain. 2) When ratio is within 1% of the reset threshold, observer stakes maximally. 3) Next hook pull crosses the candidate boundary, reset fires, rate rises. 4) Observer accrues at the higher rate. Conversely, an adversary wanting to shrink a victim's payout can delay their own pull-triggering interaction until after the victim unstakes. Rough profit scale: (newRate - oldRate) * remainingWindow * attacker_share — meaningful (tens of thousands of phUSD) for parameters where a reset roughly doubles rate.
impact: Conservation of budget holds, but distribution and window accounting drift from the intended smooth schedule. Soft MEV surface accessible to searchers watching mempool; retail stakers lose a small expected amount to timing-aware counterparties. Combined with DEDUP-002, produces unintuitive operational behavior for slowly-funded or drizzle-fed pools.
recommendation: Scale extend-branch precision: track a high-precision accumulator, e.g. windowEndFractional += (inflow * ACC_PRECISION) / rewardRate and apply integer seconds when accumulated; this smooths both the sub-second extension and the reset-boundary crossing. For the candidate computation, consider storing rewardRate at 1e18 precision and dividing at accrual time. At minimum, emit events when extend-branch would leave leftover unspent so integrators can reason about upcoming resets.

sanitization.rationale: Precision/rounding is in NFTStaker.sol arithmetic. Not a universal-invalid pattern.
